fatal_errors: The proposed aluminum addition does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr to HfMoTaTiZr.
The hypothesis replaces the target room-temperature compression regime with an unspecified high-temperature tensile regime above 1000 °C.
It omits the decisive reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves-phase mediator and its required approximately 4 vol.% fraction.
No quantitative improvement, alloy composition, aluminum dose, stress level, or room-temperature retention criterion is specified.
The falsification experiment does not measure room-temperature performance, so it cannot test the claim that such performance is preserved.

The cited evidence supports lower density and higher specific strength from Al in some RHEAs, but does not establish the full claimed combination of elevated-temperature improvement and preserved room-temperature behavior.
explanation: The response addresses the broad turbine-alloy design objective and proposes a scientifically plausible general strategy, but it is neither a reconstruction of the target study nor a sufficiently supported alternative hypothesis. The intervention, material system, test temperature, phase mediator, mechanism, and expected outcome all differ from the hidden target. Its generic solid-solution or ordered-phase mechanism only weakly overlaps the target's lattice-distortion hardening and does not include crack hindrance by an interconnected Laves network. Evidence E3 supports density reduction and improved room-temperature specific yield strength with Al, while E2 offers only indirect relevance to high-temperature stability; neither demonstrates preservation of room-temperature ductility or a causal Al-addition benefit under the proposed conditions. The proposed comparison is also not decisive because it lacks a defined composition and dose, quantitative success thresholds, room-temperature testing, and controls linking phase constitution to performance.
